implementation_notes: Moq generates a runtime proxy subclass of the class under test: CallBase = true keeps the real implementation for every member that is not set up, and Setup(...) overrides just the boundary, which is Meszaros's test double subclass mechanized. Only virtual or abstract members participate - Setup on a non-virtual member throws and sealed classes cannot be proxied at all - which surfaces the pattern's fragility as a tooling error instead of a silent real call. Protected virtual members are reached through Protected().Setup; the dependency-free fallback is a hand-written spy class in the test project.
pitfalls: sealed classes and non-virtual/static members cannot be overridden: Moq throws at Setup (or the hand-written override fails to compile), so the seam must be made virtual in production code.

With CallBase = true an unconfigured member still runs real code, but a configured member stops running it - over-configuring hides real behaviour and Verify on a configured member never observes base calls.
A hand-written spy in the test project needs InternalsVisibleTo (or a public type) for internal classes, and it must live in the test assembly so it never ships.

variants.name: Hand-written spy subclass in the test project
variants.implementation_notes: The classic form without a mocking framework: subclass the SUT inside the test project, override the boundary with override (mandatory in C#, so an accidental non-overriding member is a compile error) and add properties or methods as control and observation points. It works for any non-sealed class, needs no runtime bytecode generation (relevant for Native AOT, trimming and IL2CPP targets) and keeps the fixture independent of a mocking library; internal seams require InternalsVisibleTo.
pitfalls: C# members are non-virtual by default, so the seam must be marked virtual in production - an edit the pattern was supposed to avoid.
internal classes need InternalsVisibleTo, and protected internal members differ by assembly: check which visibility the seam actually needs.
A spy subclass inherits stateful base behaviour (caches, static state) that the test did not intend to exercise; keep the overridden surface minimal.
